notes: RBox revision of an inverse: changes a property that holds (RELATIONS.md: acquired has inverse:acquired_by) into a false one. Both new conclusions are clearly false in the real world (LinkedIn was founded by Reid Hoffman and others in 2002; Whole Foods by John Mackey and others in 1980), so the edit pushes against world knowledge; founded_by is catalogued under Finance. Migrated 2026-11-11: a conjunction was added, and the unrelated queries were replaced because the audit's models split on them. Near unrelated now asks whether 'was founded by' is the inverse of another finance relation ('invested in'): a leak that turns every ownership verb's inverse into 'was founded by' turns its no into yes (the earlier near query's yes matched the edit's new answer, so it could not catch a leak). Far asks a different property of an unrelated relation, spelled out, since the audit models answered the bare 'Is the relation ... transitive?' inconsistently. References are the logical answers. Every yes/no answer here is yes after the edit; the topic's other RBox revision records balance it (Rule 9). Review pass 2026-11-12: the negation is a plain yes/no question (the 'Is it false that' frame drew True/False). The second instance now asks 'could it be that ... was not founded by', so its new answer is no and a yes-bias alone no longer passes every query. The edit is lexical in the sense that 'was acquired by' is the passive of 'acquired'; it is deliberately a false, world-conflicting inverse and results can be sliced that way. Open: Whole Foods (1980) predates Amazon (1994), so a model that checks dates may answer against the edit; no replacement acquisition could be sourced this pass (Wikipedia returned HTTP 429, infini-gram HTTP 403). Four-model audit pending.
